headline: Congress cancels a Department of Energy rule that set stricter energy-use standards for walk-in coolers and freezers.
what_it_does: This law overturns a Department of Energy rule from December 2024 that set tougher energy efficiency standards for walk-in coolers and freezers. The rule would have limited how much energy certain walk-in doors and refrigeration systems could use each day. Because of this law, those parts no longer have to meet the new standards.

who_it_affects.group: Makers of walk-in coolers, freezers, doors, and refrigeration systems
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to redesign walk-in non-display doors by December 23, 2027, or walk-in refrigeration systems by December 31, 2028, to meet the new standards.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that buy and use walk-in coolers and freezers, such as restaurants and grocery stores
who_it_affects.how: New equipment they buy will not have to meet the stricter energy-use limits the rule would have required.
The agency's December 2024 rule is cancelled, and it cannot issue a substantially similar rule unless Congress later authorizes it.
